title: Customs
lead: Customs are the fifth of the seven ideas, and they cover how a particular group usually does things.

p: A custom is a usual way of behaving in a particular group or setting. Customs are learned through socialisation, they can differ between groups and they can change over time.
In plain words, a custom is what a particular group usually does, and it becomes a tradition when it is passed down the generations.

writers.name: Interactionists
writers.says: examine how people learn the usual ways of a group through everyday contact with its members.

list: A friendship group who usually meet at the same café after school on Fridays have a custom of their own.
A team that usually sings the same song on the bus home after a win has a custom that new players soon learn.
A friendship group that usually sends a voice note to say goodnight has a custom that belongs to that group only.
Colleagues in a workplace who usually take turns to bring in cakes on a Friday have a custom of their own.
A family that usually eats together at the table on Sundays has a custom that guests soon notice.

p: Define the term: A custom is a usual way of behaving in a particular group or setting. Customs are learned through socialisation, they can differ between groups and they can change over time.
Item link: The item describes groups developing their own usual ways of behaving. For example, a team may always huddle and sing the same song before a match, and newcomers learn this by joining in.

Explain with an example: Newcomers copying the group in the item illustrates how customs are learned by watching and joining in. A friendship group that always sends a voice note to say goodnight has a custom, not a tradition, because it has not been passed down the generations.
Theory link: Interactionists examine how people learn the usual ways of a group through everyday contact with its members.

quote.t: Groups develop their own usual ways of behaving, such as how members greet one another or what they do before a match. Newcomers learn these habits by watching other members and joining in.
